studies.Reference: Consumption of fermented milk products and breast cancer: a case-control study in The Netherlands.
studies.Authors: van't Veer P, Dekker JM, Lamers JW, Kok FJ, Schouten EG, Brants HA, Sturmans F, Hermus RJ
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Consumption of fermented milk products (predominantly yogurt and buttermilk) was measured in grams/day.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 133 incident breast cancer cases and 289 population controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The odds ratio expressed per 225 g was 0.63.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: A statistically significant decrease in breast cancer risk was observed for increasing intake of fermented milk products.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Daily consumption of fermented milk products (predominantly yogurt and buttermilk).

studies.Reference: Dairy foods, calcium, and risk of breast cancer overall and for subtypes defined by estrogen receptor status: a pooled analysis of 21 cohort studies.
studies.Authors: Wu Y, Huang R, Wang M, Bernstein L, Bethea TN, Chen C, Chen Y, Eliassen AH, Freedman ND, Gaudet MM, Gierach GL, Giles GG, Krogh V, Larsson SC, Liao LM, McCullough ML, Miller AB, Milne RL, Monroe KR, Neuhouser ML, Palmer JR, Prizment A, Reynolds P, Robien K, Rohan TE, Sandin S, Sawada N, Sieri S, Sinha R, Stolzenberg-Solomon RZ, Tsugane S, van den Brandt PA, Visvanathan K, Weiderpass E, Wilkens LR, Willett WC, Wolk A, Zeleniuch-Jacquotte A, Ziegler RG, Smith-Warner SA
studies.Journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Associations were evaluated for dairy product and calcium intakes and risk of incident invasive breast cancer overall.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: We pooled the individual-level data of over 1 million women.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: pooled HR = 0.90, 95% CI: 0.83, 0.98 comparing ≥60 g/d with <1 g/d of yogurt.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Higher yogurt intakes were inversely associated with the risk of ER-negative breast cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: P, test for trend >0.05 for all.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Risk of incident invasive breast cancer overall and by subtypes defined by ER status.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Comparing ≥60 g/d with <1 g/d of yogurt.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Insufficient studies to perform formal publication bias testing.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an effect size of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.62–1.09), indicating no statistically significant association between yogurt and breast cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by substantial heterogeneity (I² = 58.68%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.
